drafted_from: tool:turn-frames-into-slides's row in tools/turn-frames-into-slides/tool-rows.json, do-work/make-slides.mjs and test/make-slides.test.mjs; the answers were observed by running make-slides.mjs on the test's made-up board
start_here: Say to your AI: "Turn the presentation frames of my board in board.json into slides with my look, as Example deck, and put the pages in the folder out." It writes a request file and runs make-slides.mjs on your computer, then looks at every page.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads a board file and a request file on the person's computer and writes slide files into a folder.
instructions: 1. Have the board's items in a JSON file (a presentation frame is an item with extra.presentationFrame.order; every item centred inside it is on that slide) and, for your look, the values and stylesheet tool:resolve-a-look gives you.

2. Write request.json beside them: {board, title, look_values, look_css, assets: {name: file}, frames?, words_from?}. Paths are relative to the request. Use frames to make only some slides in that order, and words_from (a piece from tool:fill-a-word-template) to put filled words in place of an item's words.

3. The AI reads the tool's row with @workshop-tools tools:list {tool}, then from the root of the Workshop checkout runs node tools/turn-frames-into-slides/do-work/make-slides.mjs request.json --out out --pdf --pictures (the PDF and pictures need a Chromium; leave those two flags off without one).

4. Read the last JSON line: slides (order, label, number of items, svg path), html, and pdf and pictures when asked. Open the pictures and look at every page: text cut short ends in an ellipsis, so give that item more room.
5. If it exits 2, standard error names what to change: a look variable the look lacks, an unknown asset, a frame name that is not a frame, or frames of different sizes.

worked_examples.title: Two frames become two slides in story order
worked_examples.ask: Turn my board's frames into slides.
worked_examples.given: From tools/turn-frames-into-slides/test/make-slides.test.mjs, run for real on its made-up board: frame 'first' (order 1) holds a title 'Made for Example Co and its 70 people.' and a logo (asset mark); frame 'second' (order 2) holds a two-line body and a swatch line 'Ink is {{--ink}}.'; both frames 1280 x 720; the look has --paper #f5f1ea and --ink #202020. Command: node tools/turn-frames-into-slides/do-work/make-slides.mjs request.json --out out (no --pdf or --pictures).
worked_examples.hands_back: Last line: {"slides":[{"order":1,"label":"Slide 1","items":2,"svg":"<out>/slides/01.svg"},{"order":2,"label":"Slide 2","items":2,"svg":"<out>/slides/02.svg"}],"html":"<out>/deck.html"}, where <out> is the full path of the out folder; exit 0. Slide 1 is a 1280 x 720 page filled #f5f1ea; slide 2 shows the line 'Ink is #202020.'.

worked_examples.title: A name that is not a frame stops the run
worked_examples.given: From the test 'a request that names frames makes only those slides': the same request with frames: ["second-body"], which is a text item, not a frame. Run for real.
worked_examples.hands_back: Nothing is written. Standard error: "make-slides: frames names second-body, which is not a frame on the board." and exit 2.
